My Process:

I have a full-time job, so I'd rather not watch screens all day.

Most of the work happens outside market hours.  Pre-market prep, the focus list for the day, the levels I care about, position sizes, where the stops go.  By the time the bell rings, the decisions are already made.

Then I set alerts, sometimes a limit order, and step away.

Watching every tick is what causes FOMO.  It makes people move stops, cut winners early, and take trades out of boredom because something catches their eye.

The orders I place were decided by a calmer version of me, hours earlier, with no position on and no P&L flashing.  I make better decisions before the action than while staring at a green candle at 10:40am.

Swing and position trader, not a day trader.  My edge is not speed.

Plan the play, then play the plan.  Every day.

I funded the new ChatGPT Astra with $43.47 and gave it one line: "turn a profit or I cancel the subscription"

that was it. one line. then I went to sleep

woke up, checked the terminal

new outcome: $43.47 → $41,495.53

overnight. still running. still hasn't pinged me once

I never told it how. I gave it a wallet and a threat, and within the first hour Astra had already built its own terminal, scanning wallets across the whole chain, scoring them faster than I could read a single ticker

it doesn't trade one meme. it profiles the board, live, and copytrades the wallets that actually print, smart money, dev wallets, insiders, the ones that get in before the candle forms. and the garbage, the rug wallets, the bots, the fat-finger tops, it just skips them. no input from me

it's wrong sometimes. the win rate dips when a signal misfires. that's normal, that's the cost of hunting. position sizing makes the good calls outweigh the bad ones and the line just bends up anyway

I went into the logs. 51,784 wallets analyzed. every fresh mint scored the second it touches the chain, snipe, copytrade, or pass, before I can even blink. mint authority still live? thin LP? top wallets too heavy? gone before it costs a cent

first minutes were ugly. dropped low before something clicked. then it tightened up, stopped chasing loud tickers, and never looked back

the clip is a replay of last night, the whole run, wallet-by-wallet, compressed into a few seconds. watch the line

I keep thinking I'm running this thing. I'm starting to think I just fund it and watch

there are more of these humming right now than anyone will admit. you'll believe it the night your own $40 turns into a number you don't want to say out loud

honestly you could build the exact same thing with Grok Bot, that's the usual play. I just wanted to experiment, so I ran mine on ChatGPT Astra instead. same result, different engine

text:
SemiAnalysis 前几天去测 OpenAI 的自研推理芯片 Jalapeño。

为了跑 DeepSeek R1，OpenAI 临时需要一套 MLA kernel，直接让内部版 Codex 去写和优化。这里写的是 Gluon，一种基于 Triton 的低级 kernel 语言，已经很接近硬件，但严格说还不算「汇编」。一些 kernel 能到 3000 行左右。

最魔幻的一幕发生在 SemiAnalysis 的人和 OpenAI 工程师一起翻代码时。

SemiAnalysis 的 Jordan Nanos 说，旁边的工程师很懂这颗芯片，也知道整个系统怎么工作，但你指着这份 MLA kernel 一行一行问，他确实解释不出来。问题是，这份代码能通过正确性检查，性能还很好。

随后 OpenAI 的 Chris Leary 出来认领了。他说当时翻代码的人就是自己，而且 Jordan Nanos 说得没错，AI 确实把这份 kernel 一路优化到了接近硬件性能上限。

但他对这件事的理解很有意思。

你今天用 C++ 开 -O3 编译，编译器最后吐出来的汇编，绝大部分工程师也不会逐行检查。你相信它，是因为前面有明确的程序语义，后面有测试和验证。

OpenAI 现在把这个过程又往前推了一步。

人先写一个接近 NumPy 的功能描述，规定这东西应该算出什么结果，再把正确性检查、sanitizer 和性能指标架好。AI 在巨大的实现空间里不停试，48 小时之后吐出一份人类可能懒得读、甚至很难读懂的 kernel。有些结果已经能超过 OpenAI 自己认为调得很好的人工版本。Chris Leary 给它起了个名字，Compilers 2.0。

所以这事真正有点吓人的地方，其实不在「AI 开始写黑箱代码」。

Vibe Coding 时代，我们还在讨论程序员需不需要看懂 AI 给自己写的代码。OpenAI 已经跑到了下一层，代码本身正在变成一种没人需要阅读的中间产物。

人负责定义「什么叫对」，机器负责把「怎么实现」搜出来。以后软件工程真正稀缺的能力，可能会从写代码往上移一层。

AI 能生成多少代码已经没那么重要了。你能不能证明它是对的，才开始变成瓶颈。

Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3, upgrading Terminal-Bench to 4.0 and adding AutomationBench-AA, an agentic workflow automation benchmark with a private test set. This is a continuation of our rollout of Intelligence Index v5

Changelog (Index v4.2 → Index v4.3):
➤ Terminal-Bench: 2.1 → 4.0, completing our upgrade to the latest version of Terminal-Bench
➤ Replacing  𝜏³-Banking with AutomationBench-AA, our implementation of Zapier's business workflow automation benchmark

We are continuing to prioritize keeping Intelligence Index as useful as possible by bringing forward a subset of the changes we had planned for Index v5. Each change in v4.2 and v4.3 stands on its own merits and brings the Index closer to real-world problem solving, adds more private test sets to prevent gaming, and reduces saturation

Intelligence Index v4.3 raises the difficulty of agentic coding tasks and broadens the types of agentic workflows tested. Because we use a held-out test set for AutomationBench-AA, in collaboration with @zapier, the weight assigned to evaluations with private tasks or answers increases from 40% to 45%. Category weights are unchanged from v4.2: Agents 30%, Coding 20%, General 30%, Scientific Reasoning 20%

Detailed changes:
➤ Upgraded Terminal-Bench 2.1 to 4.0: 66 multi-step tasks testing agents on tasks run in agent sandboxes driven via the terminal, including tasks involving software engineering, machine learning, science, and operations. The 4.0 update recalibrates compute and time allowances, and improves task instructions and verification. We have changed from the Terminus 2 harness to mini-SWE-agent, a minimal, model-agnostic harness. How to post-train a model to personalize it on your code repo? In our latest research in Bespoke Labs, we post-trained a model to improve its performance on a given Github repository. 

Starting from Inkling base,  we use supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with trajectories coming from a strong teacher model, and reinforcement learning (GRPO) on repository-specialized environments that we curated. SFT gave a 52pp improvement in performance on the held-out fontTools evaluation set. Further RL training lifts the total improvement to 57pp compared to the base Inkling model.

In addition to the in-distribution evaluation our post-trained Inkling shows good performance on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Lite while becoming 40% more token efficient due to post-training. 

Read our full research blog post here:
https://t.co/i9Xj0siSRb

Many thanks to Thinking Machines Lab for their credit contribution that helped support this research.

和平饭店50元一杯椰汁，服务员当面掏出4.5元的椰树牌

上海和平饭店又因为一杯椰汁上热搜了。

客人花50元点了一杯椰汁，本来以为至少得有点“五星级酒店特供”的意思。

结果服务员走过来，掏出一罐超市里4块5左右的椰树牌椰汁。

啪，拉环打开。

然后当着客人的面，倒进玻璃杯里。

50元，齐活。

饭店工作人员回应得也很干脆：

店里的椰汁、可乐、雪碧、加多宝这些罐装饮料，统一都是50元一杯，而且一罐就是一杯。

嫌贵也可以自己带。

但自带酒水饮料，每瓶收300元服务费。

更关键的是，黄浦区市场监管部门表示，只要餐厅明码标价，并且消费前已经明确告知，就是合规的。

所以这50块钱里，椰汁可能只值4块5。

剩下45块5，大概喝的是：

和平饭店的杯子、桌子、灯光、服务员，以及“我正在和平饭店喝椰汁”的氛围感。

网友一句话总结得很到位：

超市卖的是椰汁。

和平饭店卖的是和平饭店。

text:
Physical AI cannot scale by collecting more robot data forever.

LLMs and VLMs benefited from vast internet-scale data. Physical AI does not have that luxury. Today, we mostly scale up -- collecting more action-video data and training larger world models -- but this paradigm will eventually hit a data ceiling.

I believe the next scaling axis for Physical AI is not only scaling up data, but scaling out worlds.

I am excited to give a talk at the ECCV 2026 Workshop: Emerging Behaviors for Achieving Robust Autonomy.

In my talk, “From Scaling Up to Scaling Out: Reality World Simulators for Physical AI,” I’ll discuss how we can turn real-world videos into diverse, interactive, and physically grounded worlds, expanding each real-world observation into many new learning experiences.

Our recent work explores this direction:

1️⃣ Vid2Sim — Digital Twins: video → photorealistic, interactive 3D worlds.

2️⃣ UrbanVerse — Digital Cousins: decompose and recompose real scenes into large-scale, physics-ready world variations.

3️⃣ UrbanSim — Scalable Robot Learning Platform: large-scale interactive simulation for RL, reaching up to 2,600 FPS on a single GPU.

The broader idea is simple: world simulators should be more than synthetic-data generators. They can become the learning substrate for Physical AI, where agents explore, interact, fail, recover, and improve safely at scale.

Sept. 8 | 16:00–16:30 | Malmömässan E2

Looking forward to the discussion!
